title: Tidal is banning fully AI-generated music from its platform
summary: Tidal announced Tuesday it is banning fully AI-generated music from its platform, marking one of the toughest stances a major streaming platform has made against the influx of AI tracks in recent…

image.caption: A woman walks with headphones on in New York. Streaming platform Tidal said Tuesday that as of Dec. 9, 'any wholly AI-generated track that's submitted to Tidal will be rejected and removed from our platform.' (Andres Kudacki/Reuters)

blocks.text: Entertainment

Tidal announced Tuesday it is banning fully AI-generated music from its platform, marking one of the toughest stances a major streaming platform has made against the influx of AI tracks in recent years.
Any fully AI-generated track will be rejected and removed from the platform as of Dec. 9, the company says
Tidal announced Tuesday it is banning fully AI-generated music from its streaming platform, in an update to its earlier policies aiming to protect musicians.
As of Dec. 9, "any wholly AI-generated track that’s submitted to Tidal will be rejected and removed from our platform," the company said in a statement.
"To ensure Tidal remains the best place for artists to share their work, and for listeners to enjoy it, we're removing all tracks that we determine are 100 per cent AI generated."
Tracks made with the assistance of AI will still be permitted.
Earlier this year, Tidal introduced an AI policy to clearly tag and demonetize AI-generated music, as well as a crackdown on AI-generated impersonations of artists.
Tidal's latest move to ban fully AI tracks comes amid an influx of AI-generated songs being submitted to the platform — songs that no one is listening to, the company says.

blocks.text: Tidal stated that 43 per cent of all tracks submitted to the platform over the past 90 days have been AI-generated. On Nov. 6, it reached a peak, with 60 per cent of submitted tracks flagged as AI.
"Yet Tidal subscribers are not listening to these tracks: 96 per cent of them have received zero streams in the last three months," the company said.

"It's true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fan bases. But this situation is different — at this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried."
AI-generated pop star Xania Monet hits Billboard charts
Over 65,000 tracks have been removed from Tidal to date for "suspected artist-name impersonation," the company added.
Controversy around AI music has been building in recent years, with musicians calling on platforms and governments to introduce more regulations to protect their creative output.

An increasing number of musicians have been targeted by AI bots posing as them, with some deepfakes racking up thousands of streams before being exposed, such as a 2023 AI-generated song impersonating Drake and The Weeknd. A report by 404 Media in September found that AI can also be used to insert fraudulent songs into a verified artist's real Spotify page. The streaming giant recently announced it is making its beta artist profile protection tool available to all artists by the end of the year.
Tidal is the first major music streaming platform to ban fully AI-generated music. Indie music distribution platform Bandcamp announced a ban on AI music in January.

blocks.text: Spotify currently permits AI-generated tracks, labels AI accounts as "AI Personas" and pays out royalties depending on streaming numbers, regardless of whether a track uses AI.

The company has also reported an uptick in AI-generated music flooding their service as well, noting in an October blog post that they’d taken down more than 50 million tracks they identified as "AI-generated slop and spam," in addition to 75 million "spammy tracks" they announced the removal of a year ago.
Apple Music said in August that it would roll out "Made With AI" transparency labels this year, though it's still unclear when they could hit the platform.
